what: Every line of the form `timeout .. cargo .. > log 2>&1; echo "$(date -u +%T) cargo ..: exit=$? in .."` printed `exit=0` whatever cargo returned: bash expands `$(date ..)` first and `$?` is then the status of that substitution. I told the user the workspace check exits 0 on the branch; it does not, there or on main.
cost: one false statement to the user, corrected in the same hour; the test tables were read from the result lines and are right
cause: `$?` read after a command substitution in the same word
whys: a status was carried to its report through shell text; the script was never run on a failing command; scripts-take-typed-input and the how-to on checked exit statuses say to check statuses, and nothing checks a hand-written VM script
class: an exit status that is reported without being the status of the command it names
prevention: save the status on the next line (`c=$?`) before any expansion, as verify.sh's `one()` already did; better, one runner on the VM that takes the command as a typed value and writes its status, time and load itself, so no lane writes this line by hand. Not built.
workaround: read results from cargo's own lines (`could not compile`, `test result`), which is what the tables used
